context.addApplication: Manually adds an application to DualWAN by selecting its executable file.
context.detectApplications: Finds applications available on this computer and lets you choose which ones to add to DualWAN. No routing rule is applied automatically.
context.networkActivity: Finds applications using the network during a selected time period. Network traffic contents are not inspected.
context.prefer1: Normally uses "{0}". If that connection is unavailable, DualWAN may use "{1}" for new connections.
context.prefer2: Normally uses "{1}". If that connection is unavailable, DualWAN may use "{0}" for new connections.
context.only1: Uses only "{0}". If that connection is unavailable, DualWAN does not automatically use the other WAN.
context.only2: Uses only "{1}". If that connection is unavailable, DualWAN does not automatically use the other WAN.
context.groupDecides: Does not set an individual rule. If the application belongs to an active group, it uses that group's configuration.
context.noRule: DualWAN does not force this application onto a specific WAN. Windows selects the connection normally.
context.addGroup: Creates a group that can share the same network configuration across multiple applications.
context.groupEnabled: When the group is enabled, its configuration is used by group applications that do not have an individual rule.
context.groupPolicy: Sets the group's default routing configuration. Individual application rules always have priority.
context.groupMembership: Adds the application to the group. If it already has an individual rule, that rule continues to take priority.
context.applyPreset: Quickly applies a general DualWAN configuration without manually changing each application.
context.theme: Selects the interface appearance. System follows the theme configured in Windows.
context.saveSettings: Saves the changes made to DualWAN settings.
help.what.title: What DualWAN is
help.what.body:
DualWAN lets you choose which Internet connection each application on your computer should use.

The two connections are not combined: each program uses the connection assigned to it according to the configured rules.
help.wans.title: The WAN connections
help.wans.body:
DualWAN manages two Internet connections. In this configuration, they are "{0}" and "{1}".

The names shown depend on the connections detected or configured in the program.
help.applications.title: Applications
help.applications.body:
The Applications section is the main place to choose which connection each program should use.

For each application, you can set a preference, limit it to one connection, or leave it without a specific rule.
help.individual.title: Individual rules
help.individual.body:
When you set a preference directly on an application, DualWAN creates a rule that applies only to that program.

This rule always takes priority over any configuration of the group the application belongs to.
help.groups.title: Groups
help.groups.body:
Groups let you apply the same configuration to several applications at once.

An application without its own rule uses the group's rule. If it has an individual rule, that rule is used instead.

Membership in a group is always optional.
help.preferOnly.title: Prefer / Only
help.preferOnly.body:
Prefer "{0}" normally uses "{0}", but can switch to "{1}" if the first connection becomes unavailable.

Only "{0}" uses "{0}" exclusively. If that connection is unavailable, DualWAN does not automatically use the other one.
help.failover.title: Failover
help.failover.body:
Failover is the automatic switch to the second connection when the preferred one is no longer available.

It is used by the Prefer options, while the Only options do not switch automatically.
help.wanDown.title: What happens if a connection goes down
help.wanDown.body:
If you are using Prefer, new connections can be opened on the other WAN when the main one is unavailable.

Connections that are already active, however, are not transferred automatically. A download, video call, or stream already in progress might therefore stop and need to be restarted.
help.lan.title: Local network
help.lan.body:
DualWAN does not apply Internet rules to resources on the local network.

NAS devices, printers, other computers, and local devices therefore remain accessible through Windows as usual, regardless of the WAN assigned to the application.
help.detection.title: Detect applications
help.detection.body:
Detect applications helps you quickly add applications already on your computer to the program.

DualWAN can also suggest a suitable group, but the application is not added to the group automatically and does not automatically receive a routing rule. The choice always remains with the user.
help.networkDetection.title: Network Activity Detection
help.networkDetection.body:
Network Activity Detection checks, for a period chosen by the user, which applications are using the network.

It is especially useful for finding programs that normal detection does not find.

DualWAN does not read traffic contents: it does not analyze web pages, messages, files, or other transmitted data.

Some very short connections or some system processes might not be detected correctly.
help.history.title: History
help.history.body:
History shows how the two connections are performing over time.

You can check download and upload traffic, latency, and packet loss, choosing periods of 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days.

This section helps you observe connection trends and identify possible problems or differences between the two WANs.
help.presets.title: Presets
help.presets.body:
Presets let you quickly change DualWAN's general behavior without changing every application one by one.

They can be useful, for example, when you want to temporarily favor one connection or limit the use of the other.
help.limitations.title: Known limitations
help.limitations.body:
DualWAN manages application routing but does not combine the speed of the two connections: a single connection therefore cannot use the bandwidth of both WANs at the same time.

When a rule changes or a WAN becomes unavailable, connections that are already open are not transferred automatically to the other network.

IPv6 support has not yet been fully verified. Also, some system processes shared by Windows can be difficult to attribute precisely to a single application.
help.privacy.title: Privacy
help.privacy.body:
DualWAN runs locally on the computer and does not require cloud services to manage routing or detect applications.

Network Activity Detection checks which processes are using the network, but does not read the contents of communications, messages, web pages, or transferred files.
